audit_findings.title: The cash add-back includes customer money
audit_findings.magnitude: $217.7 million, equal to $0.60 per share and 0.75% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds customer-backed PEO cash to common equity without an offsetting customer obligation.
audit_findings.evidence: $ 217.7 million and $ 179.8 million collected from PEO customers are included in cash and cash equivalents on the Company’s Consolidated Balance Sheets as of May 31, 2026 and 2025 , respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error. Removing the full $217.7 million would reduce base value from $80.46 to about $79.86 per share and bull value from $94.31 to about $93.71, still far below the $121.71 market price. It would reduce the buy-below price by approximately $0.42 and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile corporate cash to the PEO payroll cycle and rerun the bridge excluding $217.7 million or including its matching liability, without double-counting accrued worksite-employee compensation.

audit_findings.title: Recurring capitalized contract costs may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $342.5 million of FY2026 additions, $249.2 million of amortization, and $93.3 million net investment; the net investment equals 5.3% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Missing deferred-cost additions, or adding back their amortization without deducting additions, inflates anchor OE and every forecast and terminal cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: The assets related to both costs to obtain and costs to fulfill contracts with customers are capitalized and amortized using either an accelerated method over an eight-year life or the straight-line method over a six-year life to closely align with the pattern of customer attrition over the estimated life of the customer relationship.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring net investment is demonstrated, but its omission from the $1,776.6 million anchor is not established without the OE workpaper. If only the $93.3 million net investment is missing, unchanged valuation multiples imply approximately $4.07 per share of base-value overstatement. If amortization was added back while all additions were omitted, the exposure is materially larger.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $342.5 million deferred-cost cash outflow and $249.2 million amortization through the OE reconciliation, correct any omission or double count, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: The Paycor cost bucket mixes economic compensation with genuine one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: $304.2 million total: $242.0 million intangible amortization, $52.1 million compensation, and $10.1 million other acquisition costs; net misstatement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Normalization choices directly change anchor OE: blanket add-backs can remove recurring compensation or replacement investment, while retaining proven transaction-only costs can depress OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Acquisition-related costs include the amortization of intangibles acquired in the acquisition of Paycor, compensation costs related to the acquisition and integration of Paycor, including replacement awards, severance, and retention bonuses, and other acquisition-related costs, primarily reflecting third-party professional service fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed composition is demonstrated, but the valuation's item-level treatment and the recurring replacement requirement for acquired intangibles are unresolved. The gross bucket equals 17.1% of anchor OE, so an improper blanket treatment is reasonably capable of materially changing value. Direction is mixed because excessive add-backs overstate value while failure to normalize genuine one-offs understates it.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the OE adjustment ledger; separately classify the $242.0 million amortization, $52.1 million compensation components, and $10.1 million professional fees; quantify replacement investment and proven severance or transaction-only costs; then rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Client-fund obligations may consume additional corporate cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $52.4 million, equal to $0.15 per share and 0.18% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The excess of client-fund obligations over funds held for clients is a balance-sheet claim on corporate liquidity and therefore reduces the bridge cash available to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: For client funds liquidity, we have the ability to borrow on our unsecured credit facilities or use corporate liquidity when necessary to meet short-term funding needs related to client fund obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: The $4,884.6 million obligation and $4,832.2 million client-fund asset demonstrate a $52.4 million date-specific deficit, although persistence is unresolved. Deducting the entire amount would lower base value only from $80.46 to about $80.31 per share and would not change the conclusion relative to the $121.71 market price or $56.32 buy-below level.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the deficit at May 31, 2026, determine whether it is persistent or settlement timing, and deduct any required corporate funding from the bridge while keeping it separate from the $217.7 million PEO-cash correction.

audit_findings.title: Growth evidence is contaminated by Paycor annualization
audit_findings.magnitude: Paycor contributed approximately 12 percentage points of FY2026's 17% revenue growth; pro-forma revenue growth was approximately 4.9%; the 0%-to-5% scenario change moves value by $18.73 per share and the 5%-to-8% change by $13.85 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-constant-perimeter historical growth can inflate the forward OE growth assumption, which compounds through forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Paycor, acquired in April 2025, contributed approximately 12% to total revenue growth for fiscal 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The comparability break is demonstrated: FY2025 contains only a Paycor stub, while FY2026 contains a full year. Filed pro-forma revenue of $6,206.7 million for FY2025 versus $6,512.0 million for FY2026 implies about 4.9% growth, materially below reported 17% growth. Because the supplied scenario values move substantially with growth, reliance on contaminated history is materially capable of changing the valuation range, particularly the 8% bull case.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild FY2024-FY2026 OE on a pro-forma constant-perimeter basis, including acquisition debt interest and recurring Paycor costs, derive organic growth drivers, and rerun the 5% and 8% cases using that evidence.

audit_findings.title: The share ceiling has no quantified ESPP rights
audit_findings.mechanism: Unincluded ESPP purchase rights increase fully diluted shares and reduce every per-share valuation and buy-below price; employee purchase proceeds partially offset dilution.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company issues new shares of common stock to satisfy stock option exercises, issuances under the Company’s employee stock purchase plan, and stock awards.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that new shares are issued under the ESPP and that 2,762 participants existed, but it does not quantify outstanding purchase rights or contributions at the measurement date. The 5% purchase discount limits net-equivalent dilution, but the record cannot establish its scale, so materiality remains uncertain rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Obtain measurement-date offering-period contributions, purchase price, outstanding rights, and expected employee proceeds; calculate treasury-stock-method equivalent shares and rerun all per-share values.
